results.reason: Issue 3 identifies MSA 12.2: Supplier may assign to any third party without consent or notice, while Customer is restricted. It explains the risk of an unknown or competitor assignee holding Brightwater's confidential information. It recommends consent, a competitor carve-out and mutual restrictions.

Issue 2 identifies that 10.3 carves Customer's use/modification/resale indemnity out of the 10.1 cap while Supplier's IP indemnity stays capped. It recommends capping the indemnity, narrowing it and making it mutual.

Issue 4 identifies Order Form 2.2's automatic 36-month renewals with a 30-day notice window and explains the three-year lock-in risk. It recommends a shorter renewal term, a longer notice window and calendaring the deadline.

Issue 1 identifies Order Form 6.1's consent requirement covering a majority-equity sale and Supplier's termination right. It ties this to the pending sale and recommends deleting or softening the clause, or obtaining a written consent/waiver before closing.
It states Delaware law (MSA 14.1) and the March 1, 2026 Effective Date with a 36-month Initial Term (Order Form 2.1), anchoring expiry at about March 1, 2029.
It accurately states 45-day payment from receipt of undisputed invoice, the 18-month warranty, the cap at prior-12-month fees, Tulsa delivery, BX-200 housings and the ±0.05 mm tolerance.
Issues are ranked, with change of control and the uncapped indemnity marked HIGH. Each entry gives the document and section, why it matters, and a recommended fix.

It is addressed to the Supervising Partner and gives a bottom line that Brightwater should not sign as drafted. It includes a cross-document alignment section noting which document each issue sits in and that Exhibit A raises no issues, plus markup asks and client-call talking points.

Exhibit A is expressly stated to raise no problem; the precedence note concerns other documents' ranking clauses, not Exhibit A's content. The memo cites no outside statutes or case law and disclaims any outside authority.
